_comment: What each merge tool does with an EXISTING $MERGED, and how ccs may paint content into one that regenerates it. Declared facts, never inferred from the command string. Tiers: preloads | preloads-with | inject:<profile> | writes-only. `tools` is keyed by the NAME git knows (its built-ins); `executables` by the binary's basename, because a configured tool can be called anything and the behaviour belongs to the binary. A user overlay in user territory overrides entries here (merge-tools.json beside ccs-config.json).

vimdiff.why: vim opens $MERGED as a buffer; what is on disk is shown

bc.why: git's own name for BeyondCompare (the only bc-* git ships); any other name -- bc2, bc4, bc5, beyondcompare4 -- is classified by its executable below

bcomp.why: regenerates the output pane from the three inputs on every load (measured on BC5; Scooter's docs, identical for BC4)

bcompare.why: the GUI launcher of the same tool
